body:
INDEPENDENT CONFIRM, with one precision and a wider defect population.

Precision: WorldTime versus no-layer does not produce a literally equal NarrativeScene because CommonViewState and the configuration checksum retain the requested layer. It does produce the same reader-facing mark population: AtlasSpec can request only DiscourseAtlas, and AtlasCompiler emits relation-layer marks only for Reference portals plus Causal and Goal routes. A successful receipt for a request whose selected layer has no representation is still a false fulfillment unless the outcome says so.

The static population is larger than WorldTime. RelationLayer has ten cases; the Atlas build reads state.relationLayers only for Reference, Causal, and Goal. Participant, WorldTime, StateChange, Hierarchy, EntityContinuity, DiscourseSuccession, and Semantic can all be admitted into CommonViewState and bound into the receipt without a layer-specific Atlas mark or refusal. Some of their information may appear through unrelated always-on structures or policies, but that is not fulfillment of the requested layer.

Required child seam: separate requested projection capability from shared semantic selection, then account every requested layer exactly once. At minimum distinguish Produced(mark/inventory identity), EstablishedEmpty(no admissible source relations), FilteredOrSuppressed(reason and count: horizon, zoom, adjacency/layout, endpoint visibility), Unsupported(projection/layer pair), and Failed(error/receipt). A plain Right(scene) with an unaccounted requested layer is inadmissible.

WorldTime needs its own declared partial-order/chronology projection preserving context, relation status, uncertainty, and evidence; it must not be linearized into one global time axis by default. Acceptance courts should separately cover: one visible WorldTime edge on a discourse-only compiler -> Unsupported; a supported layer with zero source edges -> EstablishedEmpty; an existing edge hidden by horizon/zoom -> FilteredOrSuppressed; and a visible Causal edge -> Produced. Removing the outcome while leaving the configuration checksum distinct must fail.

So I agree with the slice boundary: this is first a storymodel4s view capability/accounting contract, then a StoryAtlas/JavaScript lowering. It is not an HTML-only task. No implementation authority inferred.
